more.summary: Invasive alien brambles have been spreading across South Africa since the early 1900s, having come from North America and Europe. All brambles fall within the genus Rubus. Their common names in South Africa are braam (Afrikaans), ijingijolo (isiZulu) and monoko-metsi (seSotho).

more.title: Researchers discover why some frogs have escaped the current amphibian mass extinction
more.summary: Amphibians are the most threatened vertebrates on Earth, with 41% of species facing extinction. In the highlands of Central and South America, a killer fungus has wiped out much of the once-abundant amphibian diversity. Yet in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, an isolated mountain range in northern Colombia, amphibians still thrive.

more.title: VCs will make billions on Anthropic’s IPO, but Amazon is set to make much (much) more
more.author: Marina Temkin
more.summary: Massive note conversions reveal the true extent of Amazon's ownership in Anthropic.

more.title: Report indicates water, food and power at risk by strong El Niño
more.summary: Rainfall reductions of up to 80% and torrential precipitation leading to severe flooding and landslides are the expected consequences across different areas of Latin America and the Caribbean from the impact of the El Niño phenomenon in 2027, according to a report co-authored by the General Secretariat of the Organization of American States (OAS), which urges member states to strengthen prevention and preparedness…

more.title: Common drugs may help dangerous viruses spread through the body
more.summary: A surprising discovery reveals that widely used anti-inflammatory drugs may unintentionally help dangerous viruses spread through the body. Scientists found that JAK inhibitors, prescribed for rheumatoid arthritis and other inflammatory diseases, can weaken a crucial immune defense against influenza, COVID-19, and other infections.

more.title: Cost overruns aren't just due to incompetence, bureaucracy and bad faith
more.summary: Nine out of 10 major transportation projects go over their initial budget. This isn't always because of incompetence.

more.title: Climate health harms outpace action, prompting calls for global health emergency
more.summary: The 2026 Report of The Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change finds that many of the health risks and harms of climate change grew faster in the decade since the Paris Agreement was introduced (2016–2025) than in the decade before it (2006–2015).

more.title: Punishment alone won't help gang‑involved teens—a former child soldier explains why
more.summary: When Americans hear of child soldiers, they may imagine tragic images of children wielding rifles on distant battlefields.

more.title: We studied 1,584 data centers—and found the buildings full of machines are tied to modest local job growth
more.summary: Data centers require enormous investments: land, buildings, computer equipment and power infrastructure. Yet, once they're up and running, they tend to employ no more than a few dozen people in occupations such as IT technicians, engineers and security guards. With billions of dollars flowing into new data centers across the United States, communities are asking what they will get in return.

more.title: Decoding the loopy physics of hula hooping with high-tech earthquake sensors
more.summary: Hula hooping may be literal child's play, but as it turns out, the physics behind the gym-class staple is so complicated that scientists have spent decades trying to understand how the hula hoop defies gravity.

more.title: The way Earth's 'thermostat' works may have changed during Pangea era
more.summary: Life arose on Earth at least 3.5 billion years ago, and our planet has remained habitable ever since—not too hot, not too cold. These life-sustaining conditions are possible in part thanks to a built-in, carbon cycle–based climate "thermostat" that controls the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

more.title: Biodiversity hotspots in southwestern Germany are losing their species richness
more.summary: Climate change and shifts in land use are affecting habitats and, consequently, plant diversity. To better understand the consequences of these developments, long-term and comprehensive data are essential. The "Floristic Mapping of Baden-Württemberg," coordinated by the Stuttgart State Museum of Natural History, provides a foundation for this.

more.title: Anduril, Qualcomm launch BlueChip, a new kind of US-made laptop
more.author: Julie Bort
more.summary: Anduril founder Palmer Luckey is vowing to bring computer manufacturing back to the U.S., and by that he doesn't just mean assembly, but every individual component, some of which are exclusively made in China today.
